Open Evening
Tuesday 15 September 5pm-7pm
We warmly invite prospective families to join us for our Middle School Open Evening and discover everything our school has to offer. Come and explore our classrooms and school environment, meet our friendly staff and talk to our lovely students. Visit exciting classrooms to find out what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow. It’s a wonderful opportunity to see our vibrant school community in action, ask questions and get a feel for life at our school. We can’t wait to welcome you!
Welcome to Broadstone Middle School
Welcome to Broadstone Middle School
At Broadstone Middle, we believe the purpose of education is to provide everyone with varied opportunities to inspire them to realise their potential. We aim to celebrate differing needs, talents and cultures. We want our learners to be confident, caring and capable citizens of the future and will strive to work with you in partnership to realise this.
Click here to access our online communication and payment system, Arbor

Broadstone Middle School is committed to provide all pupils with the knowledge, skills, inspiration and positive attitude to take ownership of their own learning and career pathways. Our careers programme ensures that all pupils are equipped with the necessary information, advice and guidance in order to be successful in their futures.
Our careers provision is delivered throughout the curriculum via PSHE lessons, Tutor times during National Careers Week (NCW), Annual Careers Fair and enrichment activities throughout the year run by external providers, such as WiseUp.
We are also committed to maximising the benefits for pupils by using a whole school approach involving parents, carers, employers, further education providers and other local agencies such as Dorset Careers Hub.
Please see our careers statement below, and a link to our Policies page where you will find the PSHE and Citizenship Policy which includes Careers.
Information on Careers Events
The students worked together in groups to solve puzzles and move themselves through different tasks including making a giant wooden dice, moving across stepping stones without letting go of them, directing each other while blindfolded without using words, and creating the longest line accross the field as they could using only what they had on them! It was a great opportunity for the students to learn to work together and get to know their new classmates ready for the coming school year.
We ran a Careers Fayre again this year, offering parents/carers and local employers the opportunity to engage with our pupils during the event on the 23rd of May 2024.
Businesses were able to set up a table/stall so that our pupils could informally approach them and talk to them personally. Employers could also run a careers activity or give an inspirational speech to the pupils during the event. This was a great way for our pupils to experience a wide range of businesses in our local community.
We are keen to encourage all our students, whatever their age, to find out as much about the world of work and future options as they can.
We ran our annual Careers Fayre event in June and offered parents/carers and local employers the opportunity to engage with our pupils during the event on the 7th of June 2023.
This event is a key part of:
Businesses were able to set up a table/stall so that our pupils could informally approach them and talk to them personally. Some employers also ran a careers activity or gave an inspirational speech to the pupils during the event. This was a great way for our pupils to experience a wide range of businesses in our local community.
Our learners in Y6 and Y8 were given an opportunity to take part in STEM activity days, the event involved 5 workshops; including Maths Roadshow, Discovering the Science of Xray and Medical models.
BCP Council came to our school and held a careers assembly for our KS2 learners
We ran our first ever Careers Fair last summer and offered parents/carers and local employers the opportunity to engage with our pupils during the event on the 8th of June 2022.
Businesses were able to set up a table/stall so that our pupils could informally approach them and talk to them personally. Some employers also ran a careers activity or gave an inspirational speech to the pupils during the event. This was a great way for our pupils to experience a wide range of businesses in our local community.
National Careers Week (NCW) is a celebration of careers guidance and free resources in education across the UK. The aim is to provide a focus for careers guidance activity at an important stage in the academic calendar to help support young people leaving education.
At BMS we ran a number of activites across the week, including teaching and non-teaching staff writing basic CV’s so that students could see the qualifications and former roles that got them to where they are now. The students took part in activities during tutor time each day including learning their interests and values, networking, vision boards and practicing interviews. Students were invited to apply to be careers champions and underwent interviews for the role resulting in 11 being chosen. The Careers Champions will help organise future events such as the upcoming Careers Fair.
In December 2021, RAF provided our Y8 students with a Virtual Realistic Job Profile (RJP) event covering a holistic overview in detail of the role and output of the RAF; all of the roles on offer, pay, terms & conditions, personal development opportunities, travel, training and sport.

The Career Lead is Mrs Penwarden, who can be contacted via email: schooloffice@bmsweb.co.uk or via telephone on 01202 696121.

We are proud to present our University of Broadstone Curriculum (UBC)
Being in your element is not only about aptitude, it’s about passion: it’s about loving what you do…tapping into your natural energy and your most authentic self. – Sir Ken Robinson
Here at Broadstone Middle, we are passionate about providing opportunities for our young learners to discover what they love and find the things they are great at. Our Broadstone University Curriculum is one way that we can provide those opportunities.
Study modules on offer:
Our University study modules offer variety and diversity, beyond the constraints of the national curriculum offered to schools. We expect our young learners to take risks and be brave in their selections, choosing new and exciting projects that they may not have tried or considered before.
The curriculum structure:
UBC takes place one afternoon per week and each module lasts 9 weeks. The final week is our showcase day where our young learners will demonstrate what they have learned. This will generally involve the community and there will be some opportunities for parents to also engage in the learning.
We will be asking your child to make their UBC choices at the start of term. A prospectus is available on our website so that you can look at take a look at what is on offer and have a conversation with your child about the modules they might choose. We ask pupils to make 8 choices and they will have the opportunity to take part in 4 of the 8 study modules they have opted for across the year.
Who knows, we might just inspire the next Bear Grylls, Barbara Hepworth or even a future Prime Minister…
